subject: Clarification: Audit log exportability, retention, and chain-of-custody
messages:
From: Rajiv Menon <rajiv.m@echostar.com>
To: priyom_das@redwood.com
Cc: Procurement <procurement@echostar.com>, security@echostar.com
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 09:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Audit logs / retention / exportability questions (RFP item)

Hi Priyom,

Thanks for the quick engagement on the RFP. A few follow-ups from our security team so we can complete section 4 (Auditability & Data Preservation):

- Retention windows: what are the default retention windows for hosted vs dedicated vs private deployments? Can retention be configured per-customer or per-log-type?
- Export formats: do you provide raw audit log exports (full event JSONL)? Do you support Parquet/CSV for analytics exports?
- Time-range slicing: can exports be sliced by arbitrary start/end timestamps (down to the second)?
- Provenance/timestamping: are timestamps RFC3339/UTC and is there monotonicity guarantees for event ordering?
- Tamper-evidence: do exports include signed manifests or checksums? Is there any signature/HSM-backed timestamping?
- Legal hold: can retention be suspended for specific resources/customer accounts to support legal holds?
- Delivery methods: what transfer mechanisms do you support (S3 cross-account copy, presigned URLs, SFTP, direct streaming)? Any throughput SLAs for bulk exports?
- Sensitive-fields: do you support PII redaction during export or is that a post-export responsibility?

We also require SOC2 evidence that the export process is auditable (controls around key management, integrity checks, access logs). I attached the RFP_LogMatrix_v3.xlsx with the exact table references. Can you respond with a short matrix and any sample artifacts?

Thanks,
Rajiv
Rajiv Menon
Sr. Manager, Security Engineering
Echostar Communications

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>

Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, Procurement <procurement@echostar.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 14:02:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Audit logs / retention / exportability questions (RFP item)

Rajiv — thanks for the detailed list. Below is a concise matrix addressing each bullet; attaching schema + a sample export manifest for illustration (appendix_a_log_schema.csv, export_sample_manifest.jsonl).

- Retention windows:
  - Hosted (Redwood API): default 13 months for audit logs, configurable up to 7 years via paid retention add-on.
  - Dedicated (reserved capacity): customer-configurable retention; typical contracts support 1–7+ years depending on SLAs.
  - Private (VPC / on-prem): fully customer-managed; retention controlled by customer policies.
  - Per-log-type: retention is configurable per-log-stream (audit, request-trace, access logs). Policies are applied at project or route level.

- Export formats:
  - Native exports: newline-delimited JSON (JSONL) with a documented schema (attached).
  - Analytics-friendly: Parquet and CSV transforms available as part of export pipeline.
  - Manifest: every export includes a SHA256 manifest and row counts (see export_sample_manifest.jsonl).

- Time-range slicing:
  - Yes — arbitrary start/end timestamps supported to the second. Exports can be incremental (since timestamp X) or full-range.

- Provenance/timestamping:
  - All event timestamps use RFC3339 in UTC. Events include both event_time (client-supplied, if present) and ingestion_time (server-assigned). Request ordering is preserved by request_id and a server-sequence field — useful for rehydration.

- Tamper-evidence:
  - Exports include SHA256 checksums per file and an overall manifest signed by service-side HMAC. For Dedicated/private deployments we can provide signed manifests using customer-rotated keys (HSM/KMS integration).

- Legal hold:
  - Legal hold can be enabled at the customer-project level to suspend deletion workflows. For hosted customers, legal hold requests are processed via our compliance flow and are retained as an immutable flag until release.

- Delivery mechanisms & throughput:
  - Supported: S3 cross-account copy (recommended), presigned S3 URLs, SFTP, and secure multipart download.
  - Throughput: export workers can saturate up to ~1 Gbps per export job depending on model of the data. For very large exports we run parallel jobs.

- Sensitive-fields / redaction:
  - Redaction: Redwood provides configurable PII redaction transforms pre-export (field-level redaction, token masking). Customers must opt-in for automatic redaction on exports; otherwise redaction is post-export.

- SOC2 evidence:
  - We can provide our SOC2 summary and control mapping (attached: soc2-summary.pdf). For evidence packages (logs of who requested exports, key rotation events, manifest signatures) we can deliver a packaged audit bundle on request.

Can you confirm the exact retention target you need (e.g., 7 years for audit events) and the delivery preference (S3 cross-account vs presigned)? If you want, we can schedule a short export test — we typically do a 72-hour sliding window export to validate config.

Best,

--
Priyom Das
Senior Solutions Engineer, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Rajiv Menon <rajiv.m@echostar.com>, priyom_das@redwood.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 15:48:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Audit logs / retention / exportability questions (RFP item)

Rajiv — a couple of operational clarifications from the platform side:

- Chain of custody & signatures:
  - For Hosted: manifests are HMAC-signed using a service key; signatures and manifest receipts are recorded in our internal audit ledger (ingest_id, export_job_id). We can export the ledger entries as part of the evidence package.
  - For Dedicated/Private: we support customer-supplied KMS keys for signing manifests (AWS KMS asymmetric keys or HSM-backed signing if requested).

- WORM / immutable storage:
  - Dedicated tenants can opt into object-lock (S3 WORM) at export landing buckets; Hosted customers can request a retention hold when we stage export artifacts in Redwood-managed buckets for delivery.

- Granularity of audit events:
  - Each audit record includes: actor_id, actor_role, request_id, route_id, model_version, ingestion_time, event_type, resource_id, outcome (success/fail), and a content-hash of the request/response (when stored).

- Access & key management evidence:
  - We capture export-request events in our internal audit trail (who requested, when, destination). KMS activity logs (key use for manifest signing) are included in evidence bundles for SOC2 queries.

I've attached the soc2-summary.pdf which maps these controls to common RFP assertions. If Echostar requires a notarized timestamp for manifests we can discuss a paid add-on for HSM-backed attestation.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Director, Platform Security
Redwood Inference

Thanks — that addresses most items. A few follow-ups before we mark the RFP section as answered:

1) We want a test export of a 72-hour sliding window (UTC 2026-08-01T00:00:00Z to 2026-08-03T23:59:59Z) to validate schema and transfer mechanics.
2) Our preference is S3 cross-account copy to this bucket: arn:aws:s3:::echostar-rfp-exports-us-east-1. We can create an IAM role if you share the trust policy.
3) We expect a transfer ETA: how long to deliver ~3 TB of logs as an estimate? Include parallelization guidance.
4) For manifests: we need per-file SHA256 and an overall signed manifest. HMAC is acceptable, but can you confirm who holds the signing key for hosted flows?

If you can kick the test and let us know credentials/role info, we'll stand up a temporary bucket and provide IAM.

-Rajiv

Rajiv — good plan. Summary and next steps below: 

Summary answers:
- Test export: we can run the 72-hour window you specified. We'll produce JSONL + Parquet outputs and the signed manifest (SHA256 per file + overall HMAC).
- Delivery: Cross-account S3 copy supported. For Hosted flows we sign manifests with a Redwood service HMAC key; metadata about signature issuance (export_job_id, sign_timestamp) will be in the audit bundle. If you prefer asym. KMS signing, we can support that for Dedicated/private deployments or contract add-ons.
- Throughput estimate: single export job can sustain up to ~1 Gbps. For 3 TB (rough calc): 3 TB = 24,000 Gbit; at 600 Mbps effective throughput we'd expect ~11 hours; at 1 Gbps ~7 hours. We will use parallelization (N workers) and multipart transfer to meet lower wall-clock time if you need <4 hours.

Action items / timeline:
1) Echostar: provide S3 role ARN or temporary credentials for arn:aws:s3:::echostar-rfp-exports-us-east-1 and confirm ACL (cross-account copy allowed). (by 2026-08-17)
2) Redwood (Priyom/Platform): schedule a test export run and share a presigned URL for the manifest and a Drive folder with export samples. (we aim to run by 2026-08-20)
3) Redwood: provide an evidence bundle (audit ledger entries + manifest signatures + KMS usage logs) after test completion. (deliverable: 2026-08-25)

Attachments included for the test and mapping: appendix_a_log_schema.csv, export_sample_manifest.jsonl, soc2-summary.pdf. I've also dropped an internal runbook link here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-Echostar-Export-Runbook and linked the HubSpot RFP record: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/echostar.

If that works I'll put a calendar block for a 30-minute sync on 2026-08-18 to coordinate roles and any firewall whitelists.

Thanks — look forward to validating.

Best,
